types.name: Merger
types.fixture_strategy: programmatic_pair — Create 2 DOCX files programmatically via Document+DocumentBuilder. Same pattern as pdf.yml merger_input_creation_lines. method: Merger.Merge(outputFile, inputFiles[])
types.primary_method_signature: static Merge(string outputFile, string[] inputFiles) -> void
types.output_validation: output file exists; size > 0; document.xml contains content from both inputs
types.blocking_resolution: Pair fixture strategy is well-understood: same as Cells 9-type pattern. DocumentBuilder creates 2 separate DOCX inputs programmatically. Taskcard can be CLOSED upon expansion.
required_constraints: REQUIRED: Merger.Merge(outputFile, inputFiles) — static call, NOT new Merger().Merge()
forbidden_constraints: FORBIDDEN: Document.AppendDocument() replacing Merger.Merge() — use LowCode Merger
types.notes: Static API — Merger.Merge(). No instance needed. Simpler than PDF Merger (no options class). Straightforward programmatic pair fixture. Lowest risk expansion candidate.

types.name: Comparer
types.fixture_strategy: programmatic_pair_with_diff — Create 2 DOCX files with different content programmatically. method: Comparer.Compare(v1, v2, outputFile, author, dateTime)
types.primary_method_signature: static Compare(string v1, string v2, string outputFile, string author, DateTime dateTime) -> void
types.output_validation: output file exists; document.xml contains revision markup (w:ins or w:del elements)
types.blocking_resolution: Same pair fixture resolution as Merger. Requires 2 programmatic DOCX inputs with DIFFERENT content for comparison to produce meaningful output.
required_constraints: REQUIRED: Comparer.Compare(v1, v2, outputFile, author, DateTime.UtcNow) — static call
forbidden_constraints: FORBIDDEN: Document.Compare() replacing Comparer.Compare() — use LowCode Comparer
types.notes: Static API. 2 inputs with different content required. Output validation: DOCX with revision markup. 16 method overloads — use simplest string-path overload.

types.name: MailMerger
types.fixture_strategy: template_docx_with_merge_fields — Template DOCX must contain documented merge field names. Simplest approach: programmatically create DOCX with merge fields via DocumentBuilder.InsertField("MERGEFIELD FieldName").
types.primary_method_signature: static Execute(string inputFileName, string outputFileName, string[] fieldNames, object[] fieldValues) -> void
types.output_validation: output file exists; document.xml no longer contains MERGEFIELD syntax; merged values present
types.blocking_resolution: Template DOCX can be created programmatically: Document+DocumentBuilder.InsertField(FieldType.FieldMergeField, false) sets merge fields. Field names must match the fieldNames array passed to Execute(). Taskcard blocking resolution: document the programmatic merge field insertion pattern.
required_constraints: REQUIRED: MailMerger.Execute(templateFile, outputFile, fieldNames, fieldValues) — static call
REQUIRED: template DOCX must contain MERGEFIELD fields matching fieldNames array
forbidden_constraints: FORBIDDEN: Document.MailMerge.Execute() replacing MailMerger.Execute() — use LowCode MailMerger
types.notes: Template fixture requires MERGEFIELD insertion. Programmatically achievable but needs explicit documentation in template_hints. Wave 3 — after Merger+Comparer validated.

types.name: Processor
types.fixture_strategy: fluent_builder — Processor uses a fluent From().To().Execute() pattern. No static call. Simplest: new Processor().From('input.docx').To('output.docx', SaveFormat.Docx).Execute()
types.output_validation: output file exists in target format
types.blocking_resolution: No fixture blocker. Processor is a universal document processor with fluent API. Primary use: format conversion (like Converter but more flexible). Decision needed: does Processor overlap with Converter? If so, should preferred_scenario differ?
types.design_question: Processor.Create().From().To().Execute() is functionally similar to Converter.Convert(). Recommended scenario: Processor for DOCX→PDF conversion with explicit fluent chain to distinguish from Converter.
forbidden_constraints: FORBIDDEN: Document.Save() replacing Processor fluent chain — use LowCode Processor
types.notes: Instance method, fluent API. 13 methods. Not static. Preferred_methods_per_type should map to 'Execute'. Wave 4 pending design decision on scenario scope.

types.name: ReportBuilder
types.fixture_strategy: template_docx_with_linq_tags — Template DOCX must contain LINQ Reporting Engine tag syntax (e.g., <<[FieldName]>>). Programmatically achievable via DocumentBuilder.Write("<<[FieldName]>>"). Data object is a simple POCO or DataTable.
types.primary_method_signature: static BuildReport(string inputFileName, string outputFileName, object data) -> void
types.output_validation: output file exists; LINQ tags replaced with data values in document.xml
types.blocking_resolution: Template can be created programmatically with literal LINQ tag text. Simple anonymous object data (new { Name = 'World' }) covers the simplest BuildReport signature. No external fixture needed.
required_constraints: REQUIRED: ReportBuilder.BuildReport(templateFile, outputFile, dataObject) — static call
REQUIRED: template DOCX must contain LINQ Reporting Engine syntax tags e.g. <<[Name]>>
forbidden_constraints: FORBIDDEN: ReportingEngine.BuildReport() — core API; use LowCode ReportBuilder.BuildReport()
types.notes: 36 static method overloads. LINQ Reporting Engine template required. Programmatically achievable but LLM must know the <<[FieldName]>> syntax. Wave 4 — high risk of LLM not knowing template syntax without few-shot example.
